doc.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997

title: Henry Mancini and the Pavarotti album
summary: Menza on working with Mancini and the story of Mancini writing Pavarotti's album.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Well this has really been fascinating. You guys have given us some great stories. I didn’t get to ask you about your L.A. days too much, but you had—
L.A. is what it is, la la.
—you had a lot of studio work.

Oh, yeah. And I have to say one of the really great thrills of my life was working with Henry Mancini, and I sorely miss him. And he was exactly like his music. He made a big influence, a huge influence on me, like so far as my writing, arranging, seeing him in front of an orchestra. The great, great story from Mancini is when Pavarotti did his movie, I asked Hank, I said, and on his birth certificate it says Enrico, his real name was Enrico. I said, “Hank,” I said, “you going to do the movie?” He said, “Oh, no, they’re going to get a classical,” you know, well John Williams did it, he wrote the songs for the © Fillius Jazz Archive -21-

movie. Three years later, we’re celebrating, my wife and I are celebrating our twenty- fifth anniversary and we’re in San Francisco. We check into the hotel and here’s this little flowers and champagne and the whole thing. And Hank calls me and he said, “You going to come with me to rehearsal?” I said, “Well Rose is with me.” He says, “I know, bring her.” He said, “I’ve got to talk to you.” I said, “You want to talk to me?” I wonder what for? He calls me when he wants to talk to me. We get in the limo and he pops a — hands me a cigar, happy anniversary, we’re drinking and Rose loved him, he was great. And he says, “I just got a call from New York, they want me to write Pavarotti’s next album.” I said, “I told you.” Well I tried to find out where they were going to do it, and I wanted to go, I wanted to be there, I wanted to be part of it, to witness it. And they wound up doing it in Geneva, Switzerland because he was performing and he was singing Balla Maschera. [phone ringing] It’s not for me is it?
You’re late for a gig. We hope not.

Anyway, the windup was he calls me as soon as he came back from the recording sessions and he says, or Rose says, “Don, it’s Hank.” I said, “Hank who?” She says, “Hank who?” She says, “The boss.” And I got on the phone I says, “Hey, how you doing, man?” He says, “Thank God I grew up in an Italian house.” I said, “Why?” He says, “I did all the right things with the music.” He said, “It was like I knew all of this all my life was coming to this.”
Oh, absolutely. And he understood it perfect. It was incredible.
He must have listened to Giuseppe Verdi now and then.
